document.title: Guardian to Keanu Factory Capture and Foundation Improvement Plan
document.summary: Introduce a privacy-aware, non-blocking capture boundary between Guardian and Keanu Factory while separating Guardian into shared gateway, local inference, and cloud inference responsibilities.

keanu_factory.role: Capture consumer, privacy processor, and dataset builder

goals: Capture eligible Guardian request and response data for dataset construction.
Keep inference available when capture is disabled, overloaded, or unavailable.
Preserve provenance across local, cloud, translated, retried, and failed-over requests.
Keep Guardian and Keanu Factory independently deployable.
Separate shared gateway, local inference, and cloud inference responsibilities.
Make capture policy, retention, privacy, and schema evolution explicit and testable.
non_goals: Guardian does not produce final ChatML or training-ready Gold datasets.
Guardian does not import or depend on Keanu Factory Python packages.
Capture does not replace Guardian usage telemetry or operational logging.
The initial implementation does not require Redis, Kafka, or another network service.
The initial implementation does not capture raw image bodies by default.
Cloud responses are not captured until provider terms have been reviewed and explicitly accepted.

architecture.boundary: versioned append-only JSONL files on the local filesystem
flow: Client request enters the shared Guardian gateway.
Guardian authenticates, normalizes, assigns a request ID, and evaluates capture policy.
The request is routed to either local or cloud inference.
Route-specific adapters attach resolved model, provider, retry, and failover metadata.
Streaming responses are reconstructed into one final semantic response.
Eligible events enter a bounded non-blocking queue.
A single background writer appends events to an active JSONL file.
Guardian atomically closes and rotates completed files.
Keanu reads only completed files and validates event schema and integrity.
Keanu applies its Privacy Gateway before producing Silver or Gold data.

event_types.request_received: Normalized request and capture-policy metadata after authentication.
event_types.request_completed: Final semantic response, resolved route, usage, and timing metadata.
event_types.request_failed: Sanitized error classification and route-attempt metadata.
event_types.request_cancelled: Client disconnect, timeout, or interrupted stream metadata.

identity.event_id: Lowercase hex-encoded SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes '{guardian_instance_id}|{request_id}|{event_type}|{sequence}'. Values must not contain the delimiter character '|'.
identity.request_id: Existing Guardian request ID or a generated UUID.
identity.client_ref: Lowercase hex-encoded HMAC-SHA-256 using GUARDIAN_CAPTURE_CLIENT_REF_SECRET as key and the authenticated Guardian key fingerprint as UTF-8 message. Never persist the raw API key, client IP, display name, or HMAC input.
identity.sequence: Monotonically increasing integer within one request.

normalization.request: Capture semantic messages after ingress normalization and before route-specific transport translation.
normalization.response: Capture the final semantic response returned to the client.
normalization.streaming: Accumulate deltas in memory and emit one completed response event instead of persisting individual chunks.
normalization.images: Replace raw image data with policy-approved metadata such as SHA-256, MIME type, byte size, and dimensions.
normalization.errors: Store stable error codes and sanitized messages without upstream credentials or raw response headers.

image_metadata.sha256: lowercase hex-encoded SHA-256 of decoded image bytes

image_metadata_rules: sha256 is required when images policy is hash_and_metadata.
mime_type and size_bytes are required when available.
width and height are optional and must be positive integers when present.
Raw base64 data and remote image query strings must not be persisted.

compatibility_rules: The schema_name suffix is the wire-contract major version; readers for guardian_capture_v1 must reject guardian_capture_v2 and later names until explicitly supported.
schema_version uses semantic versioning within one schema name and must remain in the 1.x range for guardian_capture_v1.
Readers must ignore unknown fields within a supported schema name and major schema_version.
New optional fields require a minor schema_version increment.
Breaking field or semantic changes require guardian_capture_v2 with schema_version 2.0.0.
Every event records the capture policy version used to produce it.

record_auth (optional, added 2026-08-07): per-record HMAC authentication. When GUARDIAN_CAPTURE_RECORD_AUTH_SECRET is set, each JSONL line includes a record_auth object with {alg, key_id, mac}. Keanu verifies by stripping record_auth from the parsed JSON, re-serialising, and recomputing HMAC-SHA-256 with its verification-only copy of the secret. Absence of record_auth means the feature is disabled — Keanu should fall back to file-level checksum verification.

invariants: Capture failure never blocks or changes inference output.
Authorization headers and raw API keys are never persisted.
Cloud provider credentials and environment-variable values are never persisted.
Raw client IP addresses are never persisted in dataset events.
Admin, health, metrics, embeddings, and key-management endpoints are excluded.
Every captured event remains local until Keanu privacy processing succeeds.
Only privacy-processed and validated outputs may advance beyond Bronze.

recommended_defaults.per_client_opt_in: When the global switch and route-type switch are enabled, a request is captured only if its authenticated client_ref is explicitly allowed. Per-client policy can never override a disabled global switch.
recommended_defaults.ownership_assumption: Guardian owns capture files. Keanu runs as the same Unix user or belongs to a dedicated shared read-only group; no world-readable permissions are permitted.

cloud_controls: Cloud capture requires a provider allowlist.
Provider terms must be reviewed before enabling response capture.
Cloud provenance must include provider and upstream model.
Local and cloud capture policies must be independently configurable.
integrity_controls: Use one writer and append-only file descriptors.
Prevent symlink traversal and anchor all writes beneath the configured capture root.
Write complete JSON lines and recover by discarding an incomplete final line.
Store a SHA-256 checksum for every completed rotated file.
Consider keyed record authentication after key-management and rotation rules are defined.
keanu_obligations: Run secret and PII redaction before Silver output.
Quarantine incomplete, malformed, or policy-violating records.
Prevent raw Bronze data from cloud sync and source control.
Record every accepted event in the ProcessingLedger.

rotation.trigger_logic: Rotate when either max_file_bytes or max_file_age_seconds is reached.

keanu_factory.orchestration_change: Replace the manual parser list with a typed registry and register Guardian capture ingestion.
keanu_factory.privacy_boundary: All Guardian events pass through PrivacyGateway before Silver output.

phases.name: Decisions and contracts
phases.objective: Freeze the integration boundary and safety invariants before implementation.
deliverables: Architecture decision for filesystem JSONL transport.
guardian_capture_v1 JSON Schema and representative fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: Both repositories agree on the same fixtures.
Fixtures contain no credentials or raw client identifiers.
Unsupported-version behavior is specified and tested.

phases.name: Minimal shared gateway extraction
phases.objective: Create stable capture hook points without changing runtime behavior.
deliverables: Extract request lifecycle and model routing.
Extract SSE streaming and watchdog helpers.
Keep app/proxy/server.py as the composition root.
acceptance_criteria: All existing Guardian tests pass.
Local and cloud smoke tests remain behaviorally identical.
No capture code is active yet.

phases.name: Guardian capture vertical slice
phases.objective: Capture opt-in local OpenAI chat requests safely in streaming and non-streaming modes.
deliverables: Validated capture configuration and global kill switch.
Policy engine and mandatory credential redactor.
Append-only writer, rotation, retention, and metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Capture is disabled by default.
Inference succeeds when the capture writer fails.
No auth header, API key, provider credential, or raw image is persisted.
Streaming and non-streaming requests produce equivalent semantic records.
Capture has no material p99 latency regression.

phases.name: Keanu ingestion
phases.objective: Ingest Guardian events idempotently through Keanu's modern contracts and privacy boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Reprocessing produces no duplicate records.
Malformed, incomplete, and unsupported events are quarantined.
Raw records cannot bypass PrivacyGateway.
Only completed request-response pairs become dataset candidates.

phases.name: Protocol and route coverage
phases.objective: Extend capture to all approved Guardian ingress protocols and route outcomes.
deliverables: Cancellation, timeout, retry, and failover events.
acceptance_criteria: Equivalent requests across protocols normalize to equivalent semantic events.
Provider and upstream-model provenance survives failover.
Incomplete streams never become automatic training examples.
Cloud capture remains off for providers without explicit approval.

phases.name: Guardian structural separation
phases.objective: Complete the shared, local, and cloud module separation after capture proves the boundaries.
deliverables: Config-driven provider base URLs with no duplicate hardcoded map.
acceptance_criteria: Public API behavior remains unchanged.
Shared modules do not depend on local or cloud implementation details.
Local and cloud adapters satisfy shared route contracts.
app/proxy/server.py is reduced to orchestration and router registration.

phases.name: Operational hardening
phases.objective: Prove durability, bounded resource use, and operator control under production traffic.
deliverables: guardianctl capture status, pause, resume, rotate, validate, and purge commands.
Documented restore, purge, and incident procedures.
acceptance_criteria: Disk usage remains within configured limits.
Process termination leaves at most one recoverable partial final line.
Queue overflow is visible and does not interrupt inference.
Rotation, retention, and Keanu handoff remain stable for 72 hours.

guardian_unit: Capture schema serialization and deterministic IDs.
Policy matching for client, model, endpoint, route, and provider.
Credential, PII precursor, image, reasoning, and tool redaction.
OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama stream assembly.
Rotation, retention, partial-line recovery, and path safety.
guardian_integration: Capture writer unavailable while inference remains healthy.
Client disconnect and upstream timeout lifecycle.
Secret canary scan over produced capture files.
performance: Compare capture-disabled and capture-enabled p50, p95, and p99 latency.
Load test at 100 concurrent streaming requests.
Verify bounded memory at maximum queue depth.
Verify capture stops cleanly at disk quota.

risks.risk: Credentials or secrets enter raw capture data.
risks.mitigation: Mandatory Guardian credential redaction, secret canary tests, local-only Bronze storage, and Keanu PrivacyGateway processing.

risks.risk: Cloud response capture violates provider terms.
risks.mitigation: Cloud capture disabled by default with an explicit per-provider allowlist and terms review.

risks.risk: Capture latency or failure degrades inference.
risks.mitigation: Bounded non-blocking queue, background writer, fail-open behavior, and latency acceptance tests.

risks.risk: Tool results, reasoning, system prompts, or images leak sensitive information.
risks.mitigation: Independent field policies with strip-by-default settings and Keanu quarantine rules.

risks.risk: Disk exhaustion interrupts Guardian or other host services.
risks.mitigation: Strict byte and age limits, rotation, retention, disk metrics, and capture shutdown before filesystem exhaustion.

risks.risk: Partial streams or retries create invalid or duplicate training records.
risks.mitigation: Explicit lifecycle events, deterministic event IDs, completion status, and ProcessingLedger deduplication.

risks.risk: A large refactor changes routing behavior while capture is introduced.
risks.mitigation: Use small behavior-preserving extractions and deliver one narrow vertical capture slice before broader module separation.

global_acceptance_criteria: All existing Guardian tests pass after each extraction and capture change.
Local, cloud, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama smoke tests retain their existing behavior.
No secret canary appears in any completed capture file.
Capture failures never alter successful inference responses.
Keanu reprocessing produces no duplicate dataset records.
Only privacy-processed, validated, and completed exchanges reach Gold output.
Retention, rotation, and disk limits remain stable during a 72-hour soak test.

first_delivery_slice.scope: Opt-in local OpenAI chat capture for streaming and non-streaming requests.
prerequisites: Extract only the minimum shared request lifecycle and streaming hooks.
Add secret canary and fail-open tests before wiring production routes.
first_delivery_slice.success_definition: A disabled-by-default vertical slice produces privacy-safe, idempotently ingestible local capture files without changing inference behavior or latency materially.

open_decisions: RESOLVED (2026-08-07): Multi-secret overlap period — Guardian supports GUARDIAN_CAPTURE_CLIENT_REF_SECRET (current) and GUARDIAN_CAPTURE_CLIENT_REF_SECRET_PREVIOUS (legacy) so existing opt-in client_refs remain valid during rotation. No forced re-registration.
RESOLVED (2026-08-07): Per-record HMAC — each WAL JSONL line carries a record_auth field (hmac-sha256, key_id, mac). Keanu verifies per-record authenticity, not just file-level checksums.
RESOLVED (2026-08-07): Same Unix user — both Guardian and Keanu run as the same user (flip) on the same host. File mode 0o640, directory mode 0o750, no world access.
RESOLVED (2026-08-07): Global on/off sufficient — the existing cloud_capture boolean plus the cloud_allowlist namespace filter provides sufficient granularity. No per-provider flags needed.

RESOLVED (2026-08-07): No truncation — Guardian delivers raw data without per-message/per-response size limits. Data processing (truncation, transformation) is Keanu's responsibility. File-level rotation and disk-level retention manage disk usage.

RESOLVED (2026-08-07): YAML-only — the operator who edits settings.yaml is responsible for field policy changes. No additional audit log or approval workflow. Conservative defaults protect against accidental disclosure.
